title: His father's band and its members
summary: He names the men in his father's ragtime band, says he played drums with it from about age twelve, and describes its instrumentation.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: A.J. What band did your daddy play with? I mean, do you remember any of the bands you played with? Yeah, they were on the orchestra. You ever been in line with that?

A.J. Handy's band. Yeah. I had a bass player by the name of Selby Thomas. A trumpet player by the name of Moie Melonso. A drummer by the name of Charlie Watson. A guitar player by the name of Willie Davis, but everybody called him Pick. And who else? A trombone player, Frank Toads. And then later I started playing drums with him. I played drums with him for about three years. A.J. What kind of band was it? A.J. The jazz band. A red time band they called him at the time. A.J. Did they read music? No, no, no. The way their leaders thought would follow this. A.J. What numbers did they play? A.J. Oh, now, I couldn't go back that far. A.J. What numbers they played at that time. A.J. But it was before the St. Louis Blues come out. A.J. That must have been. A.J. To think. A.J. Yeah, I was about twelve, thirteen years old when I was playing drums with him. A.J. Let me get a stride. Where were you born? A.J. In the audience? A.J. No. A.J. Born right here in Fast Christiane back on Davis Avenue. A.J.
And he had the band here, you were dating, you know? Yeah. They didn't grind at all into play? No, from here, from here in the movie he went.
He never grinded a player. Just trumpet, trombone, violin, ghetto, bass, drums.
Who played the lead? The trumpet. What did the violin play?
He was playing lead, the vocal played lead.
What time? How did you become interested in music?
